questions.question: Name the eight energy stores used in the GCSE energy model.
questions.modelAnswer: Thermal; kinetic; gravitational potential; elastic potential; chemical; magnetic; electrostatic; nuclear.

questions.question: Name the four pathways by which energy can be transferred.
questions.modelAnswer: Mechanically; electrically; by heating; by radiation.

questions.question: A falling ball speeds up. Describe the energy-store changes.
questions.modelAnswer: The gravitational potential store decreases; the kinetic store increases; some energy is dissipated to thermal stores because of air resistance.
markingPoints: some energy is dissipated to thermal stores because of air resistance.

questions.question: Explain the energy transfers when a moving car brakes.
questions.modelAnswer: Work is done by friction; energy is transferred from the car’s kinetic store; mainly to thermal stores of the brakes, tyres and surroundings; total energy is conserved.
markingPoints: energy is transferred from the car’s kinetic store
mainly to thermal stores of the brakes, tyres and surroundings

questions.question: State the law of conservation of energy.
questions.modelAnswer: Energy cannot be created or destroyed; it can only be transferred between stores.
markingPoints: Energy cannot be created or destroyed
it can only be transferred between stores.

questions.question: What is meant by energy being dissipated?
questions.modelAnswer: Energy is transferred to less useful stores, usually thermal stores of the surroundings; it becomes spread out and harder to use.
markingPoints: Energy is transferred to less useful stores, usually thermal stores of the surroundings
it becomes spread out and harder to use.

questions.question: Explain how increasing the thickness of loft insulation reduces energy transfer.
questions.modelAnswer: It traps air; air is a poor thermal conductor; a thicker layer increases thermal resistance and reduces the rate of transfer through the roof.
markingPoints: air is a poor thermal conductor
a thicker layer increases thermal resistance and reduces the rate of transfer through the roof.

questions.question: Define thermal conductivity.
questions.modelAnswer: A measure of how quickly energy is transferred through a material by conduction; a lower value means a better insulator.
markingPoints: A measure of how quickly energy is transferred through a material by conduction
a lower value means a better insulator.

questions.question: Define power and give its unit.
questions.modelAnswer: Power is the rate of energy transfer or rate of doing work; watt (W).
markingPoints: Power is the rate of energy transfer or rate of doing work

questions.question: Explain why no real device is 100% efficient.
questions.modelAnswer: Some energy is always dissipated to unwanted thermal or sound stores; therefore useful output is less than total input.
markingPoints: Some energy is always dissipated to unwanted thermal or sound stores
therefore useful output is less than total input.

questions.question: Classify coal, oil, gas, nuclear fuel, wind, solar, hydroelectric, tidal, wave, geothermal and biofuel as renewable or non-renewable.
questions.modelAnswer: Non-renewable: coal, oil, gas and nuclear fuel. Renewable: wind, solar, hydroelectric, tidal, wave, geothermal and biofuel.
markingPoints: Non-renewable: coal, oil, gas and nuclear fuel. Renewable: wind, solar, hydroelectric, tidal, wave, geothermal and biofuel.

questions.question: Compare wind power with a gas-fired power station for reliability and environmental impact.
questions.modelAnswer: Wind is renewable and produces no fuel-related carbon dioxide during operation, but is intermittent and needs backup or storage. Gas is reliable and responds quickly to demand, but is non-renewable and releases carbon dioxide and pollutants. A justified judgement should depend on purpose and location.
markingPoints: Wind is renewable and produces no fuel-related carbon dioxide during operation, but is intermittent and needs backup or storage. Gas is reliable and responds quickly to demand, but is non-renewable and releases carbon dioxide and pollutants. A justified judgement should depend on purpose and location.

questions.question: Explain why electricity suppliers use a mixture of energy resources.
questions.modelAnswer: Demand changes; some sources are intermittent; reliable sources meet base load and rapid-response sources meet peaks; a mix balances reliability, cost and environmental effects.
markingPoints: reliable sources meet base load and rapid-response sources meet peaks
a mix balances reliability, cost and environmental effects.

questions.question: A 1,200 kg car travels at 15 m/s. Calculate its kinetic energy.
A 3.0 kg object is lifted through 4.0 m. Use g = 9.8 N/kg. Calculate the increase in gravitational potential energy.
A spring with spring constant 250 N/m is extended by 0.080 m. Calculate the elastic potential energy stored.
A motor transfers 18,000 J in 30 s. Calculate its power.
A lamp transfers 1,500 J electrically and produces 240 J of useful light. Calculate its efficiency as a percentage.
questions.modelAnswer:
efficiency = useful output ÷ total input
efficiency = 240 ÷ 1500 = 0.16
percentage efficiency = 0.16 × 100
= 16%

questions.question: Describe how to determine the specific heat capacity of a metal block.
questions.modelAnswer: Measure the block’s mass. Insert a heater and thermometer and insulate the block. Record initial temperature. Switch on and measure potential difference, current and heating time, so energy = VIt. Record temperature rise. Calculate c = E ÷ (mΔθ). Repeat or use a graph of energy against temperature change. Reduce heat loss and ensure good thermal contact.
markingPoints: Measure the block’s mass. Insert a heater and thermometer and insulate the block. Record initial temperature. Switch on and measure potential difference, current and heating time, so energy = VIt. Record temperature rise. Calculate c = E ÷ (mΔθ). Repeat or use a graph of energy against temperature change. Reduce heat loss and ensure good thermal contact.

questions.question: Plan an investigation comparing insulating materials around a beaker of hot water.
questions.modelAnswer: Use identical beakers, equal water mass and equal starting temperature. Use equal thickness/area of each material. Fit lids, record temperature at fixed times and compare temperature decrease or cooling rate. Control room conditions and exposed surface area; repeat and calculate means.
markingPoints: Use identical beakers, equal water mass and equal starting temperature. Use equal thickness/area of each material. Fit lids, record temperature at fixed times and compare temperature decrease or cooling rate. Control room conditions and exposed surface area
